data.claim: SHAPES has no entry for gitlab/pypi/sendgrid/linear/digitalocean/mailgun/JWT/azure/curl -u/URL userinfo, so each sample is committed unchanged
data.falsifier: any sample in tests/test_secret_shapes_table.py is already changed on main
data.mechanism: Redactor applies only SHAPES plus session patterns; the email shape eats only the tail of a URL password
data.probe_output: 21 failed, 7 passed before adding shapes; 28 passed after
data.question: Does the log redactor leave provider tokens and URL passwords?

evidence.note: R-au-redact-shapes CONFIRMED: table test failed 21 of 28 before shapes
read brief and rules: r-everything-configurable (shapes stay in the one table behind [log].redact_builtin_shapes), r-reuse-core (one pattern set in core/secret_shapes.py, shared with REC-leak-scan)

10 provider shapes + url-userinfo in core/secret_shapes.py; tests/test_secret_shapes_table.py 28 pass, test_redact_provider_keys and test_critic_findings pass except test_a_redaction_that_errors_fails_closed (S._record missing: unrelated, fails without my change)

chunk_findings.detail: `curl-user` only matches a standalone `-u`/`--user` after whitespace, then requires `[ =]+` before the user. Given `curl -sSu admin:hunter2hunter2 https://api.example/private` (valid clustered short options) or `curl -uadmin:hunter2hunter2 https://api.example/private` (argument glued to `-u`), the engine never reaches the password class, so `hunter2hunter2` is left in the log. The new tests only feed `curl -u admin:` and `curl -s --user admin:`, so they pass while the common forms leak. Same-line `[^\n|;&]` also misses a wrapped command where `curl` and `-u` are on different lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:curl-user

chunk_findings.detail: The JWT shape requires two `eyJ` segments and a third segment of `[0-9A-Za-z_-]{8,}` with no `=`. A compact token that still has base64 padding does not match: `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIn0=.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c` fails because `=` sits between the payload and the dot, so the whole bearer stays in the log. An unsigned `alg=none` token (`eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJzdWIiOiJhbGljZSJ9.`) also fails the 8-character signature minimum, so the claims leak. `SECRET["jwt"]` only asserts the third segment of an unpadded sample is gone, so neither case is caught.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:jwt

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named and parametrized as if it checks which provider shape fired, but it only asserts `shape_hit(SAMPLES[name]) != ""`. A hit from `assigned-secret` or another row still passes, so a mis-labeled or overlapping shape is not a failure.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_secret_shapes_table.py:test_shape_hit_names_the_provider_shape

Given `curl --user=admin:hunter2hunter2 https://x.test/p`, a hit from `assigned-secret` (or any other row) satisfies the redaction test that only checks `hunter2hunter2` is gone, and this parametrize never asserts `shape_hit(...) == "curl-user"`. The previous name-check hole remains for the forms added to close the clustered/`--user=` miss.

chunk_findings.detail: `SECRETS["jwt-padded"]` is only a second `_run(43)`, not the claims. The sample is `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIn0=.` plus a signature. A redactor that blanks only the third segment leaves `eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIn0` (`sub=1234567890`) in the log while `test_provider_sample_is_changed_and_loses_its_secret` still passes. That is the claims leak the padded-JWT case was meant to lock; `jwt-unsigned` marks the payload, this sample does not.

chunk_findings.detail: The password class is `[^\s'\"]{4,256}`, so a quoted curl userinfo whose password contains a space is only partly removed. Given `curl -u "admin:hunter2 hunter2" https://api.example/private`, the match stops at the space and the redactor leaves ` hunter2"` in the log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:curl-user

chunk_findings.detail: `test_url_userinfo_password_is_wholly_removed` does not check the whole password. `URL_PASS` is `Tr0ub4dor`, `word`, and `hunter2` while the samples are `Tr0ub4dor&3`, `p%40ss@word`, and `hunter2hunter2`. An engine that dropped only those fragments would still pass, so the stated falsifier (part of the password left in the log) is not actually locked.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_secret_shapes_table.py:URL_PASS

chunk_findings.detail: The URL test only asserts the full password string is absent as one substring. Given `mysql://root:Tr0ub4dor&[REDACTED:email]/prod`, a redactor that deletes `Tr0ub4dor` and leaves `&[REDACTED:email]` makes `Tr0ub4dor&3` not in the output, so the test passes while part of the password remains — the leftover this case was meant to lock. The same split happens for `postgresql://svc:p%40ss@[REDACTED:email]:5432/app` if the match stops at the first `@`: `p%40ss@word` is gone as a contiguous string and `[REDACTED:email]` stays.

chunk_findings.detail: The `jwt` pattern's segments are `[0-9A-Za-z_-]` only, so any `=` ends the match. Given `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIn0=.dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk`, the payload's padding makes the second `eyJ…` alternative fail and the token is left unchanged, including `eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIn0` (`sub=1234567890`). Dropping the padded sample does not close that hole: a JWT the bug called out still survives in the log.
